_readme: Sūtra intellisense — read by dge/js/intellisense.js.
Turns sūtra citations in the running text into something a reader can tap, and
identifies a rule from a half-remembered name. Missing or malformed file = the
defaults below, which are what the code already does.
enabled          false switches the whole feature off.
linkNumbers      false keeps the popover and name lookup but stops marking up
references in the text.
alwaysLinkIn     grantha slug prefixes where a bare '1.1.3' is a sūtra without
further evidence. Only grammar texts by default.
cues             everywhere else a reference is linked only if one of these
words appears just before it. This is what stops a Purāṇa's
verse numbers turning into grammar links, which would be
worse than leaving them alone. Matched case-insensitively.
cueWindow        how many characters before the number to look for a cue.
identifyFromSearch  offer a matching sūtra when a name is typed into search.
analyseWords     false switches off word analysis on double-tap.
WHAT IT MATCHES BY NAME
Everything folds to a consonant-led ASCII skeleton first, so the same rule is
found from Devanagari, IAST, Kannada, Telugu, Malayalam, Bengali, Gujarati or
a rough romanisation. Vowel length, aspiration, retroflexion and sibilant
class are all deliberately discarded — someone who half-remembers a name will
not have got those right either.
'namah svasti svaha', 'नमः स्वस्ति स्वाहा' and 'ನಮಃ ಸ್ವಸ್ತಿ ಸ್ವಾಹಾ' all reach
2.3.16, नमःस्वस्तिस्वाहास्वधालंवषड्योगाच्च.
WORD ANALYSIS
Double-tapping a Sanskrit word says which stem or root it comes from and what
case, number, person or tense it stands in, then offers the dictionaries and
everywhere else in the library the word occurs.
The analysis is Vidyut's, precomputed by tools/build_morphology.py into
dge/data/_morph/ because Vidyut is a Rust binary over a 75 MB kośa and cannot
run in a browser. Coverage is real but partial: Vidyut resolves inflected
forms, not sandhi-joined ones, and the manifest records the exact figures.
A word with no analysis says so rather than pretending.
The popover also lists RELATED words — the English-Sanskrit dictionary read
backwards, so a word's entry names the others used for the same idea. Each
group shows the English sense that binds it, because inverting a bilingual
dictionary yields both true synonyms and words that merely shared a gloss;
showing the sense lets the reader tell which. Tapping one opens it in turn.
Built by tools/build_synonyms.py. It currently reads the LOCAL copy of the
reverse dictionary, which holds 1,764 of Monier-Williams' 28,238 English
headwords — the rest live in the bhumandala-kosha-data repo the live site
loads over a CDN. Point the script at a full local copy and rerun it to
cover the remainder.
Words are not marked up in the text. A page of Sanskrit with every word
underlined is not a reading experience; selection is the affordance.
THE DATA
dge/data/vedanga/vyakarana/ashtadhyayi/_index/, built by
tools/build_sutra_index.py. Rebuild it after editing the sūtrapāṭha.
The index loads only once a page turns out to cite a rule; the per-adhyāya
detail file loads only when a popover opens.
